RECOMMENDATIONS 1. Instruct the Department of City Planning, in alignment with Approach C, to initiate a code amendment for either Option 1, 2, or 3 as described herein, to upzone single family and low-density zoned parcels that are located in Opportunity Stations and in higher and moderate opportunity sites ineligible for delay within Transit Oriented Development zones and areas citywide to facilitate local implementation of SB 79; as well as 2. Instruct the Department of City Planning, to delay effectuation of SB 79 citywide, as explicitly allowed by SB 79, through the initiation of a delayed effectuation ordinance for all eligible criteria including lower opportunity areas, Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones, sites and stations meeting capacity requirements, local historic resources, Sea Level Rise Areas, Industrial Employment Hubs, and sites more than one-mile walking distance from a station. CF 25-1083 PLUM Committee Page 2 II. INTRODUCTION Senate Bill (SB) 79, the Abundant and Affordable Homes Near Transit Act, was introduced by Senator Scott Wiener and signed by Governor Gavin Newsom on October 10, 2025. The bill will become effective on July 1, 2026. On November 4, 2025, the City Council adopted a motion (Council File 25-1083), instructing various departments to prepare reports related to the SB 79 (Government Code Sections (GCS) 65912.155-162), including a request for several reports from the Los Angeles City Planning (from here on referred to as “the Department”). On November 17, 2025, the Planning and Land Use Management (PLUM) Committee discussed the Department’s first report, dated November 13, 2025, on key SB 79 provisions and options for local implementation. The subsequent PLUM Committee Report included several recommendations and was adopted by the City Council on December 2, 2025. WEBER DEPUTY DIRECTOR March 18, 2026 The Honorable City Council City of Los Angeles City Hall, Room 395 200 North Spring Street Los Angeles, California 90012 Dear Honorable Members: REPORT ON ANTICIPATED COSTS AND TIME REQUIRED FOR COURTESY NOTICES TO TENANTS AND OWNERS LOCATED WITHIN SENATE BILL 79 TRANSIT ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT ZONES; (CF 25-1083) I. SUMMARY This report provides a summary of the anticipated costs and time required to prepare and mail courtesy notifications to tenants and owners of properties located within the Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Zones as defined by Senate Bill (SB) 79. This report has been prepared for informational purposes only, with no recommended actions for the City Council, and can be received and filed. II. BACKGROUND On February 24, 2026, the Planning and Land Use Management Committee considered City Planning’s report on options to manage implementation of SB 79 and allow additional time (one year following the 7th revision of the housing element) for the City to develop a local transit- oriented development alternative plan, as permitted by the bill. Options outlined by City Planning would require the adoption of at least one zoning code amendment, or ordinance, that would be prepared and presented to the City Planning Commission this spring and subsequently presented to the City Council for adoption. During deliberations, Councilmember Nazarian inquired about the possibility of mailing notifications to properties impacted by SB 79. After clarification that the potential code amendments described in the Department’s February 18, 2026, report would not require the mailing of a public hearing notice pursuant to the Los Angeles Municipal Code, the Councilmember requested that staff provide a cost estimate for the mailing of a courtesy notice to properties impacted by the bill. The Honorable City Council CF 25-1083 Page 2 III. MAILING COST ESTIMATES AND TIMING The following outlines the estimated costs and time that would be required to mail a 5” by 8” color postcard courtesy notice to property owners and tenants located within every SB 79 defined TOD Zone. It also includes the estimated costs to additionally mail the courtesy notice to properties located within a 500-foot radius of every TOD Zone. WEBER DEPUTY DIRECTOR April 9, 2026 Los Angeles City Council c/o Office of the City Clerk City Hall, Room 395 200 North Spring Street Los Angeles, CA 90012 Dear Honorable Members: REPORT ON UPDATED ANTICIPATED COSTS AND TIME REQUIRED FOR COURTESY MAILINGS TO TENANTS AND OWNERS LOCATED WITHIN SENATE BILL 79 TRANSIT ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT ZONES; (CF 25-1083) I. UPDATED MAILING COSTS The following cost estimates have been updated to reflect updated SB 79 Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Zones as a result of the Metro Board’s selection of a Locally Preferred Alternative for the K Line Northern Extension. The estimates account for the mailing of a 5" by 8” color postcard courtesy notice to property owners and tenants located within every SB 79 defined TOD Zone, as well as properties located within a 500-foot radius of every TOD Zone. Notice to Property Owners and Tenants within all 145 TOD Zones Number of Mailers Printing Cost Mailing Cost Total Estimated Costs 714,154 $68,128 $471,341 $539,469 Notice to Property Owners and Tenants within all 145 TOD Zones + 500-foot Radius Number of Mailers Printing Cost Mailing Cost Total Estimated Costs 876,022 $83,003 $578,174 $661,177 The Honorable City Council CF 25-1083 Page 2 II. TIMING OF NOTIFICATION The time required to design, print, and mail the above-described courtesy notices is approximately 5 weeks (6 weeks if the 145 TOD Zones + 500-foot radius is selected) and would involve coordinating with the General Services Department. This would not allow for notification to occur prior to a future City Planning Commission meeting. Courtesy notices can be prepared with general information that directs recipients to City Planning’s SB 79 website, where they can find up-to-date information on the City’s actions and can look up an address to see how it may be impacted. These notices can be mailed out once funding has been allocated to City Planning and prior to City Council’s consideration of the ordinance(s). III. CONCLUSION This report has been prepared for informational purposes only, with no recommended actions for the City Council, and can be received and filed. WEBER DEPUTY DIRECTOR October 6, 2026 Los Angeles City Council ℅ Office of the City Clerk City Hall, Room 395 Los Angeles, CA 90012 Attention: Planning and Land Use Management Committee (PLUM) REPORT ON MOTION 4A FOR COUNCIL FILE 25-1083 REGARDING INITIATION OF LOCAL ALT PLAN IN RESPONSE TO SB 79 Dear Honorable Members, Introduction On March 24, 2026, the City Council adopted Motion 4a (Council File 25-1083). Directive one of this motion instructs the Department of City Planning (DCP), with assistance from the City Attorney, to prepare the necessary documents to implement a City of Los Angeles transit-oriented development alternative plan (Local Alt Plan), as authorized by Abundant and Affordable Homes Near Transit Act, Senate Bill 79, codified as Government Code Section 65912.161(a). SB 79 provides increased density, floor area ratio, height, and other incentives to encourage housing production near transit. The subject report follows the City Council’s June 23, 2026 adoption of the Low-Rise and Phased Implementation ordinances to comply with the state’s SB 79 obligations within the City of Los Angeles. The Department of City Planning is presenting information in this report to inform next steps and for further direction. PLUM Committee CF 25-1083 Page 2 The Department recommends the following: 1. Direct the Department of City Planning (DCP) to develop a Citywide Local Alt Plan and implement an equitable strategy for SB 79 capacity distribution with Department consideration of the following factors during the preparation of the Local Alt Plan: a. Analyze and recommend whether all 146 station areas are to be included or whether some station areas be subject to SB 79 outright. b. Conduct an analysis and make recommendations as to how capacity might be redistributed within, and among station areas, as limited by state regulations. c. Recommend any shifts in capacity within or between station areas using guiding indicators or qualifications for station areas and sites, as follows: i. Emphasize capacity in High and Higher Opportunity Areas and advance existing goals for Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing ii. Intensify capacity around high quality transit stations and at transit hubs iii. motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the Council instruct the Department of City Planning, Transportation Department, and the Housing Department, and in consultation with the City Attorney, and Chief Legislative Analyst, to prepare a report in 90 days on an assessment detailing the impacts of SB79. The report should include the following: • The definition of a “Transit-oriented development stop.” • Detail the applicability of SB79 to Cities neighboring the City of Los Angeles. • Detailed maps of the locations of a “Transit-oriented development stop” highlighting the one-quarter (1) mile and one-half mile (%). • Detail the allowable density per acre, height, floor area ratio (FAR) and parking. • Detail how SB79 works in conjunction with Density Bonus Law, including waivers and incentives. .• Detail how SB79 would' impact the following: Residential units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance. o Sites located within the Coastal Zone and Sea Rise areas. O Sites located within Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones. Sites located within Tsunami Zones. Me- P 1 6 2025 6 Sites located in or near evacuation routes. O Sites that have a designated historic resource either by the City, State or Federal Governments, including individual designations and Historic Districts. O Historic Preservation Overlay Zones or National Register Historic Districts (NRHD). • Details on the City's ability to delay effectuation of SB79 and on the potential development of a local "Transit Oriented Development Alternative Plan,” including but not limited to the following: O The necessary findings. O The number of “Transit-oriented development stops” that are anticipated to be analyzed. o Phasing and time requirements of delayed effectuation and Transit Oriented Development Alternative plans. • Recommendations on local implementation options including: o Detailed cost analysis, including staffing resources and consultant costs anticipated to be needed by the Department of City Planning to implement SB79, and potential resources needed for delayed effectuation, a local Transit Oriented Development Alternative Plan, and case processing. Details on how the implementation will interface with already adopted and proposed Community Plans and the Citywide Housing Incentive Program (CHIP). I FURTHER MOVE that the Council instruct the Chief Legislative Analyst, with the assistance of the City Administrative Officer, City Planning, the Department of Transportation, Bureau of Sanitation, Bureau of Street Services, Bureau of Engineering, the Fire Department, the Police Department, and request the Department of Water and Power, to prepare a comprehensive report identifying and assessing the projected impacts of SB79 density on the City’s infrastructure and utility systems including: • Costs to update, expand, and modernize the City’s infrastructure and utility systems to support projected density from SB79. • Costs to maintain expanded and upgraded infrastructure and utility systems needed to support SB79 density. Enhancements to emergency services staffing and resources necessary to support SB79 density. Citywide staffing enhancements necessary to design and deliver an upgraded infrastructure and utility enhancement plan to support new SB79 density. 0 Recommendations for mitigation, funding strategies, and any additional policy actions the City Council should consider to mitigate the effects of SB79. • Estimated increase of revenues generated from the reassessment of properties redeveloped with SB79 projects. FURTHER MOVE that the Council request the City Attorney to issue a confidential report to Council on potential legal challenges to SB79 and possible bases for cost-recovery from the state.
